answer: Before a new agent may vote or collect fees, it must finish a sequence of paid handoffs with three already-established, unrelated partners, each cleared through a monitored settlement bridge that records payer, payee, and delivery proof. Partners attach a non-transferable violet receipt only after the work lands. Receipts accumulate in a public sable archive that is costly to rewrite later. Cloning names or splitting one treasury across aliases breaks the chain and pays nothing, so mass-produced identities cannot buy many genuine crossings at once.
